NYT: "A Conspicuous Absence at the World Cup: Mexico's President"
June 11, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The NYT headline does the work: a Mexican president refusing the ceremonial throne isn't a choice, it's "conspicuous" — a thing to explain.

🇲🇽 Ticket No. 00001 went to Yolett Cervantes Cuaquehua, a 21-year-old Indigenous woman from Veracruz. The presidential balcony she skipped is the one US media keeps assigning her.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO BURIES CANADA AND CHINA IN US TRADE — $50.7B IN A SINGLE MONTH</u>

Mexican exports to the US hit $50.69 billion in April, a 21.3% annual jump and the highest single-month figure on record. Mexico captured 16.9% of all US imports versus Canada at 11.7%, Taiwan at 8%, and China down to 7.2% — its lowest position in decades.

Year to date Jan-Apr: $188.7 billion, up 9%. Trump's tariff war was supposed to discipline Mexico. Instead it accelerated China's collapse in the US market and handed the supply chain south of the Rio Grande.

Source: El Financiero (US Census data)

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ALBANIA RISES AGAINST TRUMP'S BILLION-EURO LAND GRAB</u>

Albanians are blockading Sazan Island against a Trump-Kushner megaproject — 567 hectares of protected Mediterranean coast handed to Affinity Partners and Qatari investors Moutaz and Ramez Al-Khayyat for villas and luxury hotels.

Landowners are locked out of their own land. Mediterranean monk seals and 200+ bird species are on the chopping block. PM Edi Rama: "no possibility the investment stops." Protesters' answer: "Albania is not for sale."

The same imperial blueprint Mexico has resisted on its own coastline — sold off to foreign capital under a sovereign flag.

Source: Regeneración

🔥🇲🇽 <u>ACADEMICS: MEXICO 2026 IS THE BRAZIL 2016 PLAYBOOK</u>

Contralínea panel with UNAM Latin Americanists Aníbal García Fernández and Marcela Román lays out the parallels: media manufacturing a chaos narrative, lawfare attempts, orchestrated street protests, all timed to a World Cup cycle — exactly how Dilma was unseated.

"No crisis in this century can be understood at merely the national level," García Fernández argues. The 2024 judicial reform — popular election of federal judges — is what blocks the Sergio Moro route from repeating in Mexico.

The script is the same. The defenses are not.

Source: Contralínea

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE SOFT-COUP MAP AGAINST SHEINBAUM — NAMES, NETWORKS, FUNDING</u>

A new Contralínea investigation by Aníbal García Fernández traces the operation: Calderón, Fox, Taboada, Marko Cortés and PAN brass coordinating with Atlas Network, NED, USAID, MCCI, México Evalúa, Konrad Adenauer, CPAC, and Students for Liberty.

USAID kept funding 35 Mexican NGOs in 2025 after its official "closure." The international cast — Milei, Díaz Ayuso, Sergio Moro, Iván Duque — is the same one deployed against every progressive government in the region.

This is not domestic opposition. It is regime-change architecture, documented.

Source: Contralínea

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>US AND CANADA DENIED VISA TO PALESTINE FOOTBALL PRESIDENT</u>

Jibril Rajoub, head of the Palestinian Football Federation, made it to Mexico City for the World Cup opening — Mexico granted him a visa. The US and Canada refused.

"They did not grant me a visa for the United States after I requested it in Amman. Their behavior is ridiculous," Rajoub told AFP. In April he refused to take a group photo with the Israeli federation at the FIFA congress in Vancouver. Now the co-hosts are punishing the sport for the politics.

Mexico hosted him. The empire blocked him.

Source: La Jornada

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM ON CHAOS PLOTTERS: "THE IMAGE TO THE WORLD IS JOY"</u>

Despite a coordinated push by opposition bots, conservative NGOs, and US-backed influencers to portray Mexico as in chaos before the World Cup opening, Sheinbaum told the mañanera: "No se le cumplió a aquellos que querían mostrar a México en caos; la imagen al mundo es de alegría."

Mexico beat South Africa 2-0 in front of a packed Azteca. Fans flooded the Zócalo. The chaos narrative died on live TV, broadcast to billions.

Source: La Jornada

🇲🇽🛢️ LATIN AMERICA WILL DELIVER 51% OF NEW GLOBAL OIL SUPPLY IN 2026 — EIA

According to US Energy Information Administration projections cited by El Financiero today: global crude production will grow ~800,000 barrels/day in 2026 — and Brazil, Guyana, and Argentina alone will deliver 410,000 of those barrels. That's 51% of the world's entire production growth coming from just three Latin American countries.

The three combined hold only 5.5% of global market share, but one out of every two new barrels arriving on world markets in 2026 will be Latin American. Brazil's offshore deepwater drove monthly output above 4 million bpd for the first time in October 2025; Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale and Guyana's Stabroek block are the other engines.

While Washington bombs Iran and tries to choke Hormuz, the energy axis is quietly migrating south. The world buys from whoever pumps it.

Source: El Financiero
